content: The amount of medicine in your body should be maintained at a consistent level for optimal effectiveness. It is crucial to continue taking this medication for the entire duration prescribed by your doctor, even if your symptoms improve or disappear after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects of this medication may include headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach upset, fatigue, dizziness, or difficulty sleeping. It is important to remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections of the mouth or vagina). Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Precautions: Before starting griseofulvin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness or impair your alertness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects, making you more dizzy or less alert. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication unless your doctor permits it. Drinking alcohol during treatment with this drug may result in a rapid heartbeat and skin flushing. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using griseofulvin, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable forms of birth control with your doctor while using this medication and for one month after your last dose. If you become pregnant, contact your doctor immediately to discuss the risks and benefits of continuing this medication. The effects of this drug on human sperm are unknown, but based on animal studies, the manufacturer recommends waiting for a period of time after completing treatment before attempting to father a child. It is also unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Usage and Storage: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and medical tests (such as kidney/liver function tests and complete blood counts) should be conducted while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about ways to manage the infection and prevent reinfection, as fungi spread easily in warm, moist environments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
